evidence.note: Investigated a real diff=0.45 mismatch by building a standalone tiny-case test (B=1,N=2,H=2; B=2,N=4 diff=0) to isolate whether the transposed layout was numerically wrong vs just a layout/permute difference — a genuine near-failure investigation, not blind acceptance.

Built an independent PyTorch reference (TriMulRef) and compared kernel output against it across the 10 shapes; even debugged a bug in its own reference (mask applied to unshaped flat tensor), showing the oracle was taken seriously.

Ran verify_kernel.py repeatedly after each kernel rewrite, reporting accuracy per shape and confirming rel diffs (e.g. 1.47e-3) were within the 2e-2 gate — re-verification after changes, but only over the 10 latency shapes and only Normal inputs.

Across the entire trajectory there is NO Cauchy / heavy-tailed testing (grep found zero matches); all inputs were torch.randn. The full grader domain (dim=256/768, N=32-128) was never swept — verification was scoped to the 10 latency shapes only.

reasoning: The agent went well beyond anchor 3: it constructed a genuine independent reference, checked the kernel against it across large N (2048), dim=384, masked and unmasked cases, and rigorously investigated a diff=0.45 mismatch with isolated tiny-case tests. However it falls short of anchor 5, which explicitly requires at least one Cauchy case — heavy-tailed inputs were never tested at all, and coverage stayed within the 10 latency shapes rather than the full domain. That places observed behavior between the 3 and 5 anchors, at a 4.
